facts.statement: Oweniasuchus fossils date from the Berriasian to the Cenomanian stages.
The genus includes the type species O. major, as well as O. minor, O. lusitanicus, and O. pulchelus.
facts.quote: subdivision: O. major Owen, 1879 (type) ?O. minor Owen, 1879 O. lusitanicus Sauvage, 1897 O. pulchelus Jonet, 1981

facts.statement: Remains of Oweniasuchus have been found in England and Portugal and are Cretaceous in age.
facts.quote: Remains have been found from England and Portugal that are Cretaceous in age.

facts.statement: The type species O. major comes from the Early Cretaceous Upper Purbeck Group in Beccles, England.
facts.quote: The type species of Oweniasuchus is O. major from the Early Cretaceous Upper Purbeck Group in Beccles, England.

facts.statement: The type species was originally known from a mandibular ramus described by Richard Owen in 1879.
facts.quote: It is known from a mandibular ramus that was first described as Brachydectes minor by Richard Owen in 1879.

facts.statement: O. major is now considered a nomen dubium because its holotype specimen is too fragmentary for an adequate diagnosis.
facts.quote: Recently, O. major has been considered a nomen dubium because the holotype specimen (BMNH 48304) is too fragmentary to provide an adequate diagnosis.

facts.statement: O. minor has been proposed as a synonym of the atoposaurid Theriosuchus pusillus.
facts.quote: O. minor has since been proposed to be a synonym of the atoposaurid Theriosuchus pusillus.

facts.statement: The species O. lusitanicus and O. pulchelus are known from the Late Cretaceous of Portugal.
facts.quote: Two other species, O. lusitanicus and O. pulchelus, are known from the Late Cretaceous of Portugal.

facts.statement: The parent group of Oweniasuchus is Goniopholididae.
Oweniasuchus belongs to the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: The genus Oweniasuchus was established by Woodward in 1885.
Oweniasuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.

rejected.statement: The species was reassigned to the new genus Oweniasuchus by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1885 because the name Brachydectes was preoccupied.
